text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- Provincial and municipal deficits have already been reduced in the run-up to European Monetary Union. Ewald Nowotny, financial spokesman for the Social Democrats, expects the government's budget plans for 1996 to be on target regardless of whether Creditanstalt is privatised.
- Austrian industry remains pessimistic over long-term economic prospects.
- Conservative People's Party wants to remain the strongest party in Austria after winning European Parliamentary elections on October 13.
- Austria's central bank is at the centre of discussions between the ruling parties over the next candidate for governor, to be replaced next year.
- Politicians criticize synthetic fibre maker Lenzing's plans to cut some 500 jobs.
- Initial agreements over longer shopping hours between employer's and employee representatives are looking promising.
- Even though the industry's economy is looking better, some three percent of jobs have been cut. Export is seen as the basis for economic development.
- Rent for offices have gone down 25 percent in prime locations.
- The disputed plans to put specialist doctors on call duty only over holidays and weekends could save hospitals one billion schillings, hospital managers say.
- Rail maker VA Schienen, a unit of VA Stahl, looks set to receive major orders from Slovakia, Slovenia and Turkey.
